sub_scenario.one_line: genomics bioinformatician: poor seat fit as configured

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the pipeline scripts and closing stale entries.
The QA checklist review wrapped early today.
Lab meetings and journal clubs in the busy seminar room cost my work nothing.
Someone new shadowed me in the genomics annex this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the variant calls into one message before lunch.

The sample-swap I caught last year, the one that would have invalidated the cohort, surfaced during quiet-annex QA; my checklist depth simply collapses in noisy settings, and my own review notes say so.
The annex is where the deep catches happen.
Where all of them have happened.
Routine pipeline reruns and monitoring can happen at any desk, noisy or not.
I archived last cycle's notes on the QA checklist and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
The principal investigator credits that catch with saving the entire grant renewal.
The deep-QA work has grant-level stakes.
A vendor call about the pipeline scripts ran long but ended well.
I walked through the genomics annex checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the variant calls.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the QA checklist records and fixed it at the source.
My two trial weeks at the bench-side hot-desk row, beside the sequencer alarm consoles, logged three near-miss QA slips that only the second reviewer caught.
The row produced a near-miss cluster immediately.
I sketched next week's plan for the variant calls before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the pipeline scripts updates.
The seating reshuffle assigns bioinformatics permanently to that same bench-side row.
The lab manager says sitting with the wet-lab team is how computational people stay grounded.
Framing my QA slips do not share.
I closed the week by updating the genomics annex handover notes.
The seating plan is being finalized this week. Is the bench-side row the right seat for my QA role as things stand?
